commit.message:
Rint G2 general gate (Codex 10-15 recheck Q7, first author approved 10-20): membrane values r_face must be finite and non-negative before assembly, tests first; update the short Codex recheck request (same-class hardening ratified, Q7 implemented in this commit) and the progress records

iface_require_quantitative checked the row fingerprint but not the membrane values, and the assembly only
applies a film where r_face > 0, so a plan whose fingerprint was recomputed after setting one film row to
NaN or a negative value silently dropped the film, and +inf zeroed the face.  The gate now requires every
axis row's r_face to be finite and >= 0 right after the fingerprint check (r = 0 and cut tombstones allowed),
so solve_sigma_z refuses before assembly.  The gate only runs when an iface plan is passed; the iface-off
path is unchanged.  step3_sigma.py is outside the sealed 32 files.

- test_rint_g2_am_iface.py new case Q7 (4 checks): NaN / -r_face / +inf film row with recomputed fingerprint
  = gate ValueError naming r_face and no CG call; positive controls RRM r = 0 plan, normal RRM plan (Codex
  values, rel 1e-9), CNC r = 0 plan bit-identical to OFF, finite positive mutation passes and solves.
  Unfixed code 133/136 (the three must-raise checks), fixed 136/136.
- test_rint_g2_rrm.py N9b split: the cut-deletion bypass (finite values, still outside the general gate)
  keeps its recorded sigma; the film-NaN plan must now be refused by the general solver, with the blocked
  bypass size recorded through the registered r = 0 plan (same assembled matrix).  Unfixed 54/55, fixed 55/55.
- Unfixed counts re-verified by unpacking the tests-only state into a new empty folder.
